description: B5's managed key-store spec -> algorithm table. Each entry answers one question: if a KMS reports a key under this provider-native spec string, which algorithm and which stated key size does the provider's own documentation say it is? Data, not code, for the same reasons crypto-packages.json is (C1's rule, and check:standards polices its retrievedAt dates).
criticalCaveat: This table reports what a key IS, never what it protects. A KMS export lists the keys the provider holds; it does not say which data, service or TLS endpoint each key stands behind, and nothing here should be read as a claim about blast radius. It is also second-hand evidence: the submitter's export is taken at its word, and no credential ever reaches this product to check it against the live key store.
curationRules: `algorithm` must be a canonicalName in algorithms.json, so algorithm-mapping.ts resolves severity, replacement and standard for it at read time. Asserted in algorithm-mapping.test.ts.

A key spec whose primitive algorithms.json does not catalogue gets `algorithm: null` and a `noAlgorithmReason`, NOT the nearest catalogued name. The key is still counted and named in the ingest response, so a KMS holding only HMAC keys reads as 'examined, nothing reportable found' rather than as un-examined. Inferring AES from Azure's `kty: oct` is the same manufactured finding crypto-packages.json refuses for JWT libraries.

`keySize` is the size the provider's own documentation states for the spec. Where the spec does not state one (Azure `kty`, Vault `hmac`, every post-quantum parameter set) it is null — never an assumed default. G-05.

`retrievedAt` lives once per provider, on the documentation page that was actually opened, not once per spec row. Four pages were read; dating eighty-odd rows individually would claim eighty-odd retrievals that never happened.

Curve bit sizes are NOT duplicated here for providers that name a curve in a separate field (Azure `crv`). Those resolve through named-curves.ts, which every other collector already uses — one curve name means one bit size across every surface.

statusValues.verified: A verbatim quote from the provider's own documentation supports the claim, read on the provider's `retrievedAt`. It does NOT mean the key was inspected: this product never holds a credential for the key store.
statusValues.needs-check: No supporting quote was obtained. Carries no `retrievedAt`, because there is no re-verification date to age out — dating an unverified claim is exactly the failure check:standards cannot see.

aws-kms.keySpecField: KeySpec (the DescribeKey/CreateKey response field; the CustomerMasterKeySpec member carries the same value and is deprecated)
aws-kms.keyIdField: KeyArn, or KeyId within a single account and region

citation.document: AWS Key Management Service Developer Guide — Key spec reference

aws-kms.note: In China Regions SYMMETRIC_DEFAULT is a 128-bit SM4 key, not AES-256 — quoted below. This table cannot tell the two apart from a key spec string alone, so a China-Region export is mis-sized by it; the region is recorded on the observation so a reader can see which case they are in. Tracked in the report's Pending list.

azure-key-vault.name: Azure Key Vault / Managed HSM

citation.document: Azure Key Vault REST API — Get Key (JsonWebKeyType / JsonWebKeyCurveName definitions), api-version 2025-07-01

azure-key-vault.note: Azure is the reason this table resolves a curve separately from a key spec. A JsonWebKey states `kty` and, for EC, `crv` — but it has NO key_size member (the RSA modulus length is only implicit in the base64url `n`), and the list-keys operation returns only `kid` and `attributes`. So an Azure RSA key legitimately arrives with a known algorithm and NO stated size, and this table records null for it rather than assuming 2048. That is G-05 in its purest form.

keySpecs.quote: AES-128 wrapped with GCM using a 96-bit nonce size AEAD (symmetric, supports derivation and convergent encryption)
keySpecs.rationale: The documented description states AES and the 128-bit key length.

keySpecs.quote: AES-256 wrapped with GCM using a 96-bit nonce size AEAD (symmetric, supports derivation and convergent encryption, default)
keySpecs.rationale: The documented description states AES and the 256-bit key length. This is Vault transit's default type.

keySpecs.quote: ChaCha20-Poly1305 AEAD (symmetric, supports derivation and convergent encryption)
keySpecs.noAlgorithmReason: algorithms.json catalogues the quantum-vulnerable and classical-hygiene algorithms this product reports on, and has no entry for this primitive. Naming it anyway would put an algorithm on an asset that no mapping can resolve a severity, replacement or deadline for.
keySpecs.rationale: ChaCha20 is defined with a 256-bit key (RFC 8439), so the size is reportable even though the algorithm is not catalogued.

keySpecs.quote: ED25519 (asymmetric, supports derivation). When using derivation, a sign operation with the same context will derive the same key and signature; this is a signing analogue to convergent_encryption.
keySpecs.rationale: Ed25519 is EdDSA over a 256-bit curve — the same resolution named-curves.ts makes for the name ed25519.

keySpecs.quote: ECDSA using the P-256 elliptic curve (asymmetric)
keySpecs.rationale: The documented description states ECDSA and the curve; P-256 is 256 bits.

keySpecs.quote: ECDSA using the P-384 elliptic curve (asymmetric)
keySpecs.rationale: The documented description states ECDSA and the curve; P-384 is 384 bits.

keySpecs.quote: ECDSA using the P-521 elliptic curve (asymmetric)
keySpecs.rationale: The documented description states ECDSA and the curve; P-521 is 521 bits.

keySpecs.quote: RSA with bit size of 2048 (asymmetric)
keySpecs.rationale: The documented description states RSA and the bit size.

keySpecs.quote: RSA with bit size of 3072 (asymmetric)
keySpecs.rationale: The documented description states RSA and the bit size.

keySpecs.quote: RSA with bit size of 4096 (asymmetric)
keySpecs.rationale: The documented description states RSA and the bit size.

keySpecs.quote: HMAC (HMAC generation, verification)
keySpecs.noAlgorithmReason: algorithms.json catalogues the quantum-vulnerable and classical-hygiene algorithms this product reports on, and has no entry for this primitive. Naming it anyway would put an algorithm on an asset that no mapping can resolve a severity, replacement or deadline for.
keySpecs.rationale: Vault's `hmac` type takes a key_size parameter that the type string does not carry, so no size is reported from the spec alone.

keySpecs.quote: External key via Managed Keys feature (enterprise only)
keySpecs.noAlgorithmReason: A Vault managed key is backed by an external HSM or cloud KMS. Vault states only that the key is external, so naming an algorithm would be a guess about a system this export cannot see.
keySpecs.rationale: A managed key is held in an external HSM/KMS; Vault's transit key type states neither algorithm nor size.
